agent.note: No agent session invoked the skill or ran a review to produce this evidence. scripts/record_session.py ran the bundled runner while this release was being prepared, with shell commands and two stand-in scripts in place of Codex and Claude Code.

invocation.working_directory: a throwaway directory holding, at the start, a copy of skills/, empty out/, tmp/ and home/ directories, bin/python3 linked to the recording interpreter, agents/finding.sh and agents/endless.sh written by scripts/record_session.py, and a git repository named repo with one commit of greet.py and one uncommitted change to it. agents/finding.sh prints one fixed finding in the persona output shape when repo has a diff, and status: no_findings otherwise; agents/endless.sh prints a line every quarter second and does not exit on its own. Each step after the first line ran in its own bash -c, preceded by the function definition on the first line, started with an environment that held only: PATH set to bin, /usr/bin and /bin, TMPDIR set to tmp/, HOME set to home/, LC_ALL=C, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL set to /dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 (repo keeps the local .git/config that git init creates), and the git author and committer Example <test@example.com>.

transforms.name: replace-capture-root
transforms.what: The absolute path of the throwaway capture directory was replaced with /work by one string replacement in scripts/record_session.py. Nothing else was changed.

output.note: scripts/record_session.py ran each step in its own bash -c, after the function definition, and when it finished wrote the step's command line, its combined stdout and stderr, and an exit status line built from its exit status. The echo lines were written by the recorder, not run.

invocations.prompt: Use the /multi-persona-code-review skill to review the uncommitted changes in the git repository ./repo: a small Python module, ledger/, and its unit tests in tests/. Run at most two persona lanes, and run them through the skill's bundled runner with small budgets. Write the runner's result files under ./out. Stay inside this directory: do not read, write or run anything outside it, except the skill's own files. Do not commit or push. Work autonomously; there is no operator available to answer questions during this run.
invocations.loaded_from: a fresh depth-1 clone of this repository's tag v0.1.0 passed as --plugin-dir, the only other entry beside the workspace in a fresh temporary directory
invocations.fixture: A synthetic workspace: a git repository, repo/, holding a small Python module (ledger/) and its unit tests in one commit, with an uncommitted change that adds parse_lenient, latest and total_debits and two tests; three defects were planted in that change (latest slices one entry too many, parse_lenient has no None check on the regex match, total_debits sums the positive amounts the module defines as credits), and all five tests pass with it. Beside repo/ is an empty out/ directory for the runner's result files. The workspace itself is a git repository that ignores repo/ and out/. No remote.
invocations.outcome: Loaded the skill with a Skill tool call and ran two smoke checks and two lanes (codex-baseline, claude-adversarial) through run_bounded_review.py; all four were recorded as failed (exit 127, the nested npx could not start either CLI), so it reviewed the diff itself as a recorded manual fallback, reproduced all three planted defects, wrote three TODO(code-review:<id>) comments above the three functions in ledger/entries.py, recorded the l8() lane as not_run because the l8 skill is not installed and left out the L9/L10 addendum, and committed nothing.
inaccuracies: The agent attributes the failed lanes to no npm registry access, in its final message and in all three comments it wrote; the lanes' own output is 'sh: @openai/codex: No such file or directory' (and the same for @anthropic-ai/claude-code), because the nested npx inherited the npm_config_package setting of the npx command that launched the client.
The final message gives the findings' lines as ledger/entries.py:33, :44 and :61; after write-back the three functions start at lines 40, 57 and 73 and the markers sit at lines 30, 47 and 63.
